title: Grilled Salmon Caesar with Charred Romaine
changes_from_base: Grilled salmon fillets turn it into a main course, and the romaine halves and bread are charred on the grill instead of tossed with croutons.
summary: A grill-pan Caesar: romaine halves charred until smoky, served with crisp-skinned salmon fillets, grilled baguette and a lemony Parmesan dressing.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
romaine hearts, halved lengthways through the core

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the mayonnaise, Parmesan, lemon juice, tamarind, garlic, oil and pepper. Set 4 tbsp aside for brushing.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Brush the bread with the olive oil and the cut sides of the romaine with 2 tbsp of the reserved dressing. Season the salmon with the salt and brush with the rest of the reserved dressing.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Heat the grill or griddle until very hot. Toast the bread 1-2 min per side and char the romaine cut side down for 1-2 min. Grill the salmon flesh side down first, 3-4 min per side, until it flakes and reaches 63 °C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Arrange the romaine, salmon and toasts on plates and spoon over the remaining dressing.

tips: Oil the grill well and do not move the salmon until it releases by itself.
Char the romaine only briefly; the centre should stay crisp.
Salmon is safe at 63 °C; take it off a little earlier if you prefer it moist and pink.
storage: Best on the day. Leftover salmon keeps 1 day in the fridge; eat it cold. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
